findings.description: The user_data script contains hardcoded AWS access key ID (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA) and secret access key (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) in plain text. These credentials are readable by anyone with describe permissions on the instance and are committed to source control, which must be treated as compromised.
The EC2 instance's root volume is not configured with encryption enabled, leaving the underlying block storage unencrypted at rest.
The instance is launched in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled, exposing it directly to the internet.
The EBS volume is created without the encrypted attribute set to true (commented out in the configuration), leaving stored data unencrypted at rest.
The EBS snapshot is created without encryption, so the snapshot data is stored unencrypted at rest, which also exposes it during copy or restore operations.
The security group admits SSH traffic (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, granting the entire internet access to the management interface, enabling brute-force and unauthorized access to the instance.

The security group allows all outbound traffic (from_port 0, to_port 0, protocol -1) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration path and a channel to command-and-control infrastructure.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs is created without default encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS) enabled, leaving log data stored unencrypted at rest.
